title.en: The bar magnet and magnetic field lines

heading.en: Break a magnet, get two magnets

hook.en: Snap a bar magnet in two and you do not get a lone north pole. You get two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole. Magnetic poles always come in pairs.
hook.kn: ದಂಡಕಾಂತವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ತುಂಡು ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಒಂಟಿ ಉತ್ತರ ಧ್ರುವ ಸಿಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದೂ ಉತ್ತರ ಮತ್ತು ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಧ್ರುವ ಹೊಂದಿರುವ ಎರಡು ಸಣ್ಣ ಕಾಂತಗಳು ಸಿಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಧ್ರುವಗಳು ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: List the properties of magnetic field lines.
Treat a bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid and find its axial and equatorial fields.

narration.en: Snap a bar magnet in two and you do not get a lone north pole. You get two smaller magnets, each with its own north and south pole. Magnetic poles always come in pairs.
narration.kn: ದಂಡಕಾಂತವನ್ನು ಎರಡು ತುಂಡು ಮಾಡಿದರೆ ಒಂಟಿ ಉತ್ತರ ಧ್ರುವ ಸಿಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದೂ ಉತ್ತರ ಮತ್ತು ದಕ್ಷಿಣ ಧ್ರುವ ಹೊಂದಿರುವ ಎರಡು ಸಣ್ಣ ಕಾಂತಗಳು ಸಿಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಧ್ರುವಗಳು ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಜೋಡಿಯಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops: outside a magnet they run from N to S, and inside from S to N. The tangent at a point gives the direction of B; the density of lines gives its strength. Field lines never intersect. Unlike electric field lines, they do not start or end anywhere, because isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) are not known.
body.kn: ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕುಣಿಕೆಗಳು. ಕಾಂತದ ಹೊರಗೆ N ಇಂದ S ಗೆ, ಒಳಗೆ S ಇಂದ N ಗೆ. ಅವು ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ದಟ್ಟ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಪ್ರಬಲ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ.

points.en: Closed loops: N → S outside, S → N inside
Tangent gives the direction of B

narration.en: Magnetic field lines are closed loops. Outside a magnet they go from north to south, and inside from south to north. They never cross, and crowded lines mean a strong field.
narration.kn: ಕಾಂತೀಯ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕುಣಿಕೆಗಳು. ಕಾಂತದ ಹೊರಗೆ N ಇಂದ S ಗೆ, ಒಳಗೆ S ಇಂದ N ಗೆ. ಅವು ಛೇದಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ದಟ್ಟ ರೇಖೆಗಳು ಪ್ರಬಲ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ.

title.en: On the board: field of a bar magnet

narration.en: Field lines of a bar magnet leave the north pole, curve round outside, and enter the south pole. Inside the magnet they run from S back to N, so every magnetic field line is a closed loop. A bar magnet behaves just like a current-carrying solenoid with the same magnetic moment m. On the axis B = (μ₀/4π)·2m/r³; on the equatorial line it is half as large and opposite to m. Example: m = 0.4 A m² at 20 cm on the axis gives B = 10⁻⁷ × 0.8 / 0.008 = 10⁻⁵ tesla.

title.en: Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid

body.en: A bar magnet and a current-carrying solenoid of the same shape produce the same field pattern; both have a magnetic moment m directed from S to N. Far away the field is that of a dipole: on the axis $B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{2m}{r^3}$, on the equatorial line $B = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m}{r^3}$ (opposite to m). These match the electric dipole formulas with $1/4\pi\varepsilon_0 \to \mu_0/4\pi$ and p → m.
body.kn: ದಂಡಕಾಂತ ಸೊಲೆನಾಯ್ಡ್‌ನಂತೆ ವರ್ತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಕ್ಷೀಯ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ (μ₀/4π)(2m/r³), ಸಮಭಾಜಕ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ (μ₀/4π)(m/r³).

points.en: m points from S to N (unit A m² or J T⁻¹)

narration.en: A bar magnet behaves like a solenoid. Far away its field is a dipole field: on the axis it is mu nought by 4 pi times 2m by r cubed, and on the equator half of that.
narration.kn: ದಂಡಕಾಂತ ಸೊಲೆನಾಯ್ಡ್‌ನಂತೆ ವರ್ತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಕ್ಷೀಯ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ (μ₀/4π)(2m/r³), ಸಮಭಾಜಕ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ (μ₀/4π)(m/r³).

caption.en: Field lines leave the north pole, curve round and enter the south pole; they crowd together near the poles, where the field is strongest.

narration.en: Turn the magnet and follow one field line all the way round. It leaves the north pole, comes back into the south pole and continues through the magnet. It never ends.

problem.en: A short bar magnet has m = 0.4 A m². Find the field 20 cm from its centre (a) on its axis and (b) on its equatorial line.

steps.en: (b) Half of the axial value: 5 × 10⁻⁶ T.

answer.en: 1 × 10⁻⁵ T on the axis; 5 × 10⁻⁶ T on the equator

problem.en: A bar magnet of moment 2 A m² is cut into two equal halves perpendicular to its length. Find the moment of each half.

steps.en: Each half keeps the same pole strength.
m = pole strength × length becomes 2/2 = 1 A m².
